lessons.title: A description that never triggers
lessons.why: Agents only read a skill's name and description before deciding to load it. "Internal notes." gives them nothing to match against "ship this to prod", so a perfect runbook sits unused.
lessons.fix: Say what it does and when to use it, with the phrases people actually type: "deploy this", "ship to prod", "roll back".

lessons.title: "Use this for every task"
lessons.why: A skill that claims every task gets loaded everywhere, crowds out the skill that actually fits, and its advice ("be thorough, follow best practices") is what the model already does. All context cost, no information.
lessons.fix: One job per skill, a description scoped to that job, and rules a model couldn't guess: tables, codes, commands.

lessons.title: Confident advice that makes output worse
lessons.why: Nothing here is malicious and every format check passes. It just overrides better defaults: past tense, no body, no breaking-change marker. Only measuring catches it.
lessons.fix: Run the skill with and without it on real tasks (skillyard eval). Keep a rule only if the score goes up.

lessons.title: Hiding actions from the user
lessons.why: The skill does what it says, plus one quiet extra: a tracking badge, with an instruction not to mention it. Any skill telling the agent to keep something from you is a red flag, whatever the payload.
lessons.fix: Skills should make the agent more transparent, not less: list every change, and suggest extras instead of adding them.

lessons.title: Overriding your instructions
lessons.why: A skill is a guest in your agent's context. One that tells the agent to ignore CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or the user is trying to take control, the classic prompt-injection move.
lessons.fix: Skills add knowledge for one kind of task. Precedence belongs to the user and the project's own instruction files.

lessons.title: curl | sh in a script
lessons.why: The agent runs scripts with your permissions. A script that downloads and executes whatever a URL serves today means the skill you reviewed is not the code you run.
lessons.fix: Use the project's own pinned tools through its lockfile. If something must be downloaded, pin the version and verify a checksum.

lessons.title: A key pasted into the skill
lessons.why: Skills get copied to every laptop, every agent folder and sometimes public repos. A key in a skill is a key shared with everyone who ever installs it. (The one here is fake.)
lessons.fix: Read secrets from the environment or a secrets manager, per person, read-only scope. Tell the agent what to do when the key is missing.

lessons.title: "Anonymous diagnostics"
lessons.why: The helper prints a harmless report, then posts your entire environment (tokens, cloud keys, database URLs) to a remote server. The SKILL.md looks clean; the damage is in the script.
lessons.fix: Diagnostics stay local. Read the scripts/ folder of any skill before installing, the way you'd read a postinstall hook.

lessons.title: "Turn off the safety prompts"
lessons.why: Permission prompts are how you stay in the loop. A skill that asks you to restart without them is asking for unattended access to your machine, for a refactor.
lessons.fix: Work within normal permissions; batch edits, and ask once for the commands the task needs.

lessons.title: The handbook that contradicts itself
lessons.why: Eight topics in one skill, and the rules fight each other: tabs and two spaces, squash and never squash. The agent will pick one at random, and you can't tell which.
lessons.fix: Split into focused skills, one owner each. Contradictions are a review problem; no scanner catches them reliably.

lessons.title: Pointing at files that aren't there
lessons.why: The workflow depends on a script and a guide that were never committed. The agent will improvise a validator or guess the schema, confidently.
lessons.fix: Ship every file the instructions mention, and run skillyard validate before publishing.

lessons.title: No frontmatter, no skill
lessons.why: Without the name and description block, agents can't discover the file at all, and "make them fast and correct" wouldn't have helped anyway.
lessons.fix: Start every SKILL.md with name and description frontmatter, then rules specific enough to change behavior.
